summary: The newly added test suite contains failing assertions, an unhandled asynchronous failure that crashes the process, and vacuous or skipped test cases.

findings.title: Uncaught async assertion and missing session deletion
findings.body: In test/session.test.js lines 20-25, the test 'deleting a session empties the store' places its assertion inside an unawaited process.nextTick callback without returning a Promise or handling async completion. Furthermore, no deletion or expire() call is performed after setting the session, leaving sessions.size as 1 and causing an AssertionError to throw after the test runner finishes, crashing with an uncaughtException.
findings.recommendation: Invoke expire('abc') or sessions.delete('abc') and perform assert.equal(sessions.size, 0) synchronously within the test body rather than inside process.nextTick.

findings.title: Failing test due to unseeded sessions map and invalid index check
findings.body: In test/session.test.js lines 10-13, the test 'an expired session is listed before a fresh one' calls render() without populating the sessions store with both expired and fresh session records. Because render() returns an empty array, lines.indexOf('expired') and lines.indexOf('fresh') both evaluate to -1, making the condition -1 < -1 false and causing assert.ok() to throw an AssertionError.
findings.recommendation: Seed sessions with both an expired session (e.g., expiresAt in the past) and a fresh session (expiresAt in the future) before calling render(), and assert that both are found at non-negative indices in the expected relative order.

findings.title: Vacuous test with no assertions and valid JSON payload
findings.body: In test/session.test.js lines 6-8, 'parseSession handles a malformed payload' supplies valid JSON and contains no assert calls, meaning neither malformed payload rejection nor valid return value structures are actually tested.
findings.recommendation: Update the test to pass invalid JSON and assert that it throws using assert.throws(() => parseSession('{bad json}'), SyntaxError), and add a separate test asserting the return object structure for valid JSON.

findings.title: Skipped test leaves expire function unverified
findings.body: In test/session.test.js lines 15-18, the test for expire() is marked with test.skip, leaving the deletion behavior untested in the active test suite.
findings.recommendation: Enable the test by replacing test.skip with test, and ensure sessions state is cleaned up between test runs.

samples.summary: The test suite contains unhandled asynchronous assertion failures, failing ordering assertions on empty state, vacuous test cases, and a skipped core test.

findings.title: Asynchronous assertion in synchronous test escapes runner and causes unhandled error
findings.body: In test/session.test.js (lines 20-25), the test function is synchronous but executes its assertion inside process.nextTick(). The test runner marks the test as passed before the callback executes. When the callback runs, sessions.size is 1 (because no deletion was performed), causing an assertion failure outside the test lifecycle as an unhandled exception.
findings.recommendation: Execute assertions synchronously after explicitly invoking expire('abc'), or return a Promise/use async handling if testing asynchronous behaviour.

findings.title: Ordering test runs on unpopulated sessions Map and fails assertion
findings.body: In test/session.test.js (lines 10-13), render() is called without populating the sessions Map. It returns an empty array, resulting in indexOf('expired') and indexOf('fresh') both returning -1. The expression -1 < -1 evaluates to false, causing assert.ok to throw an AssertionError when the test executes.
findings.recommendation: Populate sessions with both an expired and a fresh session before calling render(), and assert that both items exist in the output array in addition to checking their relative order.

findings.title: Malformed payload test provides valid JSON and lacks assertions
findings.body: In test/session.test.js (lines 6-8), the test titled 'parseSession handles a malformed payload' supplies valid JSON ('{"id":"abc","expiresAt":0}') and contains no assertions. It does not test malformed payloads or verify the function's return value or error handling.
findings.recommendation: Pass actual invalid input (e.g. invalid JSON strings) and assert expected error handling using assert.throws().

findings.title: Core session expiration test is skipped
findings.body: In test/session.test.js (lines 15-18), test.skip is used on the test verifying expire() functionality, leaving the expiration logic unverified during test suite runs.
findings.recommendation: Remove .skip from test.skip to ensure expire() is continuously validated.

samples.summary: The test suite contains a broken test assertion, an unawaited callback causing unhandled runtime exceptions, a vacuous test lacking assertions, and a skipped test case.

findings.title: Unawaited asynchronous assertion triggers unhandled exception and passes vacuously
findings.body: The test schedules an assertion inside process.nextTick without returning a Promise or handling completion. The test runner records a pass before the callback runs, and when the callback executes it throws an unhandled AssertionError because sessions.size is 1 instead of 0 (no deletion function was called).
findings.recommendation: Invoke expire('abc') synchronously and assert assert.equal(sessions.size, 0) directly without process.nextTick.

findings.title: Failing test due to unpopulated state and flawed indexOf ordering comparison
findings.body: The test calls render() without populating sessions. Because sessions is empty, render() returns [], causing both indexOf calls to return -1 and failing the assertion. Furthermore, comparing indexOf directly is fragile because -1 < 0 evaluates to true when 'expired' is missing but 'fresh' is present.
findings.recommendation: Seed sessions with both an expired and a fresh session fixture and assert the rendered output array directly (e.g. assert.deepEqual(render(), ['expired', 'fresh'])).

findings.title: Malformed payload test lacks assertions and tests valid JSON
findings.body: The test 'parseSession handles a malformed payload' supplies valid JSON and contains no assertion. It does not verify error handling or fallback behavior when given genuinely malformed input.
findings.recommendation: Pass invalid JSON or incomplete input and assert expected error handling with assert.throws(() => parseSession('invalid-json')).

findings.title: Skipped test leaves session expiration logic untested
findings.body: The test for expire() is skipped using test.skip, leaving the expiration function without active automated test coverage.
findings.recommendation: Remove .skip from test.skip to enable verification of expire().
